candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preconception care, pregnancy-related health promotion, and preventive teaching
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — folic acid and neural-tube-defect prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the CDC's routine daily folic-acid recommendation for women capable of becoming pregnant.

options.A: Get 400 micrograms of folic acid every day
options.B: Use folic acid only when actively trying to conceive
options.C: Wait until pregnancy is confirmed before starting folic acid
options.D: Use folic acid only when there is a family history of neural tube defects

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends that all women capable of becoming pregnant get 400 micrograms of folic acid every day. Daily folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects and should not be delayed until pregnancy is confirmed or limited only to people with a family history. A is correct for the general population; individuals with special risk factors may require individualized clinician guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends 400 mcg of folic acid every day for all women capable of becoming pregnant to help prevent neural tube defects.
candidate.source_document_title: Folic Acid: Sources and Recommended Intake
candidate.source_locator: Overview — CDC recommends all women capable of becoming pregnant get 400 mcg folic acid daily; Supplements — daily vitamin with 400 mcg
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse provides preconception health teaching to women capable of becoming pregnant. Which folic-acid recommendation is appropriate for the general population?
